verdict.reasoning: Patient reports a “really, really strong headache” with “my vision is a little bit blue flourish… quite blurred… some zigzag lines,” indicating severe headache with visual changes.

Doctor confirms: “this morning… about four hours ago, you've developed a headache on the left side of the head,” and earlier asks “was it a sudden onset headache?” Patient replies “Yeah, yeah, yeah,” supporting sudden onset this morning on the left side.
Pain score: “let's say that that's 10 I have now maybe five. Well, six.” Non‑response to paracetamol: “I tried paracetamol but didn't work. To be honest. I feel exactly the same.”
Patient: “My vision is quite blurred… some zigzag lines kind of,” and earlier: “I feel like dizzy.” This supports blurred vision, zigzag lines, and dizziness.
Patient: “definitely I vomit twice… As soon as the headache started, I also vomited… and I still feel nausea.”
Patient: “I feel that this can be some kind of brain tumor or something… Or maybe a stroke… you definitely start to wonder if I should go to A and E urgently.”
Patient references prior kidney stones: “Well, I had the kidney stone, so let's say that that's 10,” and doctor: “You've mentioned in the past you've had kidney stones.”
Doctor: “Do you take any regular medications?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “Are you allergic to any medications?” Patient: “Not that I'm aware. Yeah, not that I'm aware.” This supports no known drug allergies.
Patient: “My mother has migraines.”
Patient: “And also, I have hypothyroidism in the family… She also has hypothyroidism.”
Doctor summarizes: “you're feeling dizzy as well, but you've got no neurological symptoms. You're walking fine,” indicating no neurological symptoms reported on this (history-based) assessment.
Doctor asks about walking and concludes: “when you're walking, you're able to walk fine in a straight line… Not really… you're walking fine,” indicating intact walking ability.
Doctor: “it sounds like what you're suffering from is what's known as a migraine.” This is a working/possible diagnosis.

Doctor explains why: “it’s on one side of the head… you've got blurry vision… with the nausea and vomiting… very typical of a migraine.” Dizziness is also noted earlier. This supports migraine based on unilateral headache, visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting, and dizziness.

Doctor: “I would recommend in the time between now and when we can see you take some medications, maybe something like ibuprofen. … ibuprofen with an anti sickness which you can get from the pharmacy.” This is ibuprofen and an antiemetic.
Doctor: “And also to drink a sugary carbonated drink, something like coke.”
Doctor: “Then we can go up the treatment ladder. You can get specific migraleve medication.” This implies considering Migraleve if initial measures are insufficient.

Doctor: “if that doesn't work, we would want to see you as soon as possible to do like a full neurological exam as well… we could see you today at some point.” This is a follow-up appointment for full neurological exam if no improvement.

Doctor: “if you do take these medications and… you feel much better on yourself, you can cancel it. You can give us a call and cancel it.” This instructs the patient to monitor symptoms and cancel the appointment if improved.
